newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares ease on profit-taking after records.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares ease on profit-taking after records.

text.p: 1025 GMT - Istanbul shares slipped in quiet profit-taking on Friday morning after a firm opening, brokers said.
* The IMKB National-100 ended the session at 1,907, down five points, or 0.26 percent from Thursday's all-time high close of 1,912. It moved between 1,900 and 1,936 in the session.

The index hit two record closes in the past two days as well as on Monday amid positive expectations that a newly formed right-left coalition government will win a confidence vote in parliament on July 12.
* Morning volume firmed to 15.20 trillion, up 29 percent from 11.74 trillion on Thursday.

"There was profit-taking in the second half of the session, but I expect an upward correction in the afternoon with selective activity. The index may test 2,100 levels next week with intermittent profit-taking," said Mustafa Toprak from Es Securities.
Brokers said lower-than-expected June inflation data encouraged purchases at the opening.

Turkey's wholesale prices rose 3.4 percent and consumer prices climbed 2.9 percent in June, down from 5.2 and 4.7 percent, respectively in May, and compared to market expectations of 3.4 - 4.5 percent.

* Of the 247 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 112 to 68 while 67 remained unchanged. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.22 percent to 1,794, the IMKB Services gained 0.11 percent to 1,866 and the IMKB Financial lost 0.52 percent to 2,088.
Leading actives were state owned flat steel producer Eregli, down 250 lira to 24,500 and state oil refiner Tupras, up 1,000 lira to 89,000.
